method: The 89 events of 2026-07-v1, carried over verbatim and unedited, plus 80 assembled on 2026-07-30 by six further INDEPENDENT research passes, one per world region (sub-Saharan Africa; North Africa, the Levant, Turkey and the wider Gulf; central and eastern Europe, the Baltics and the Balkans; south and south-east Asia; Latin America and the Caribbean; Central Asia, the Caucasus, greater China and the unsampled European markets). Each pass was run in isolation from the others and forbidden from consulting this tracker, its database, its repository or asktherecruiter.com; discovery was public web search and the publishers' own pages only, in local languages as well as English. Every item was fetched from the publisher's own page and confirmed for company, date, country and amount before it was written down, and every source URL was then re-checked for reachability before the set was sealed. One item was dropped for an unreachable URL and nothing was dropped on any other ground; nothing was added, edited or removed after matching began. v1's window is kept deliberately, so the widened result is directly comparable with the 9.0% published against v1 on the countries the two share.
caveats: The window ends on the day of the first measurement, so events announced in the last two days had almost no time to be collected. That makes the result slightly pessimistic at the tail rather than flattering.
Some countries carry only one or two events, so a single country cell is an indication and not a rate.
The set counts announced events. A funding round disclosed only in a later filing, and a leadership change announced internally first, are both out of scope here.
Three rest-of-world items are debt facilities rather than equity rounds, which some readers would not count as a funding round at all.
This measures two of the four kinds of signal the tracker collects, funding rounds and leadership changes. Pay and ways-of-working signals are not tested here and their coverage is unmeasured.
Eighty nine events is enough to separate the big categories and not enough to say anything reliable about a single country.

The widening is a SUPERSET of 2026-07-v1, so 89 of the 169 events have been measured once already. Their result against v2 is partly a re-measurement, and only the 80 new events are being asked for the first time.

Fifty of the 80 new events come from countries that were not in v1 at all, so most of the new geography carries one or two events and is an indication rather than a rate. The regional totals are what can be read; the country cells mostly cannot.

Coverage of the new regions reflects which publishers allow an automated fetch as much as where events happened. Every research pass reported the same obstruction: national dailies in Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Rwanda and Greece, and the disclosure portals of the Indonesian, Malaysian, Sri Lankan, Kuwaiti, Athens and Johannesburg exchanges, refuse a fetcher outright. Real events were found there and dropped unverified, so those countries are under-represented in the set and their recall will look better than it is.

Announcement date and effective date diverge sharply outside the US and western Europe, most visibly in African leadership changes, which are often announced weeks before they take effect. This set uses the announcement date throughout, which excluded several otherwise valid events.

Ten funding events carry amount_disclosed=false because the publisher stated no figure. They are held to the same standard on every other field, and their amount cannot contribute a defect either way.

items.detail: Nepal's Machhapuchchhre Bank promoted Prasiddha Raj Aryal to Senior Deputy Chief Executive Officer and Subash Jamarkattel to Deputy Chief Executive Officer, following a board decision on Shrawan 4, 2083 (20 July 2026).
items.verified: Fetched the article dated 21 July 2026; it confirms Prasiddha Raj Aryal's promotion to Senior Deputy CEO and Subash Jamarkattel's to Deputy CEO at Machhapuchchhre Bank, decided by the board on Shrawan 4, 2083.

items.detail: Malaysian insurtech PolicyStreet raised an additional US$5 million from BlueOrchard (Schroders Group), topping up its Series C to US$26 million alongside existing backers Khazanah Nasional, Cool Japan Fund, Altara Ventures and Gobi Partners.
items.verified: Fetched the article dated 14 July 2026; it confirms the additional $5 million from BlueOrchard bringing Series C to $26 million, and identifies PolicyStreet as Malaysia-based.

items.detail: Philippine commerce infrastructure startup Etaily raised an undisclosed round from Malaysia's Vynn Capital to fund expansion into Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, following a late-2025 round led by SMBC's Asia Rising Fund.
items.verified: Fetched the article dated 2 July 2026; it confirms Vynn Capital's investment in 'Philippine commerce infrastructure startup Etaily', states 'financial terms of the investment were not disclosed', and references the prior SMBC Asia Rising Fund round.

items.detail: Dhaka-based deep-tech company Dubotech, founded by alumni of BRAC University's BRACU Duburi underwater-vehicle team, raised US$350,000 led by Agile Minds Solutions with reinvestment from Horizon Investments to build autonomous underwater, ground and aerial systems.
items.verified: Fetched the article dated 14 July 2026; it states Dubotech, 'a Dhaka-based deep-tech company building underwater, ground, and aerial autonomous systems, has raised US$350K in funding led by Agile Minds Solutions, with reinvestment from Horizon Investments'.
